key_insight: Electrolyte conditioning preserves high structural validity but increases repetition and reduces distinct polymers satisfying combined design requests, despite slightly improving predicted property error.
engineering_relevance: Polymer design workflows should evaluate distinct usable candidates and chemical constraints alongside property accuracy.
method: A 38.3-million-parameter decoder-only Transformer generates polymer repeat units.
Optional controls specify property targets, chemical-feature inclusion or exclusion, and electrolyte-domain conditioning.
Evaluation compares generation conditions using the validation-loss-selected model and examines nine checkpoints.
evidence_signal: At a Tg target of 246.11 K, adding electrolyte conditioning reduced predictor-estimated MAE from 26.97 to 26.07 K, but distinct valid yield within 50 K fell from 82.35% to 32.31%, and training-catalog-unseen yield fell from 59.90% to 19.71%.
watch_item: Predicted Tg and structural validity do not establish experimentally verified electrolyte performance.
paper_title: PolyGPT: A Decoder-Only Transformer for Polymer Electrolyte Design
